items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: It came out that Robeson was a Communist. >> Was a Communist.

ctx.x: It came out that Robeson was a Communist.

Was a Communist. And it really caused a stink. So I went to the same writers of the newspapers, and I told them what had happened. And I says, as far as I'm concerned, there's the contract, and I tore it up, I will not be there. And that's how I broke with them. They stopped giving me jobs. But they were really on my tail.
You said that the telephone in the Jazz Record was --

items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses a concert produced by 'The Young Women of America' featuring Paul Robeson, and his subsequent refusal to perform there due to Robeson's political associations, but does not indicate a personal relationship with Robeson himself.

ctx.x: Obnoxious, I don't know who they are, but they give me a deposit, a union contract. They hire me and I got Max Kqminsky and I got Chippy Hill, I got -- and I go to the newspapers and I get a plug in the columns. In a week, I see an ad in the paper: The Young Women of America who so success-
fully produced the Paul Robeson concert in New Jersey. That was a riot in New Jersey, that concert. It was a big riot and a lot of problems.
It came out that Robeson was a Communist.
